page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores using hyperthreading, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache. It delivers 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature dedicated GPU hardware, relying on external network storage. Its baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results reveal a divergence between single-threaded and parallel processing capabilities. Single-core performance falls on the lower end, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 893.0 and a single-core stress-ng result of 1108.98. However, multi-core throughput scales to mid-tier levels, achieving 5757.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests and 11776.53 in stress-ng multi-core testing. In-memory and caching metrics demonstrate stable throughput, with uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 75.3 GB/sec, write bandwidth reaching 53.85 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput recording 11.19 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration provides high RAM capacity relative to CPU resources, delivering cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high single-thread clock speeds. Because local storage is absent, storage throughput and latency depend entirely on external block storage services. Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is best suited for in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, medium-scale relational and NoSQL databases, memory-resident analytics pipelines, and general enterprise data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores, 128.0 GB of RAM, and 35 MB of L3 cache, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations reflect modest single-threaded performance alongside balanced multi-core execution, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5757.0 and Redis throughput reaching 11.19 million SET operations per second. Memory throughput remains consistent, delivering 75.3 GB/sec in uncached block reads. Due to its dense memory allocation and reliance on external network volumes, this instance is suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, in-memory databases, caching layers, and distributed data processing systems.
